docs.title: Development Guide
docs.text: This guide provides instructions for setting up the development environment and contributing to the molecular-analyzer project.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
1. Clone the repository: bash git clone https://github.com/shahjalal2313/molecular-analyzer.git cd molecular-analyzer
  2. Create and activate a virtual environment: bash python -m venv venv source venv/bin/activate # On Windows use `venv\Scripts\activate`
  3. Install dependencies: bash pip install -r requirements.txt pip install -r requirements-dev.txt

docs.title: Running Tests
docs.text:
To run the test suite, use pytest:

pytest

docs.title: Coding Style
docs.text:
We use black for code formatting and flake8 for linting.

black .
flake8 .

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: Please see our Contributing Guidelines for details on how to contribute to the project.

docs.title: Contributing to Molecular Analyzer
docs.text: First off, thank you for considering contributing to Molecular Analyzer! It's people like you that make open source such a great community.

docs.title: Where do I go from here?
docs.text: If you've noticed a bug or have a feature request, make one! It's generally best if you get confirmation of your bug or approval for your feature request this way before starting to code.

docs.title: Fork & create a branch
docs.text:
If this is something you think you can fix, then fork the repository and create a branch with a descriptive name.

A good branch name would be (where issue #38 is the ticket you're working on):

git checkout -b 38-add-feature-x

docs.title: Get the test suite running
docs.text:
Make sure you're running the test suite locally before you start making changes.

pytest

docs.title: Implement your fix or feature
docs.text: At this point, you're ready to make your changes! Feel free to ask for help; everyone is a beginner at first 😸

docs.title: Make a Pull Request
docs.text:
At this point, you should switch back to your main branch and make sure it's up to date with the latest upstream version of the repository.

git remote add upstream git@github.com:shahjalal2313/molecular-analyzer.git
git checkout main
git pull upstream main

Then update your feature branch from your local copy of main, and push it!

git checkout 38-add-feature-x
git rebase main
git push --set-upstream origin 38-add-feature-x

Finally, go to GitHub and make a Pull Request

docs.title: Keeping your Pull Request updated
docs.text:
If a maintainer asks you to "rebase" your PR, they're saying that a lot of code has changed, and that you need to update your branch so it's easier to merge.

To learn more about rebasing and merging, check out this guide from Atlassian: https://www.atlassian.com/git/tutorials/merging-vs-rebasing

docs.title: 📖 Molecular Analyzer User Guide
docs.text: Welcome to the comprehensive user guide for Molecular Analyzer! This guide will help you get the most out of the platform's molecular analysis and visualization capabilities.

docs.title: 🎯 Table of Contents
docs.text:
1. Getting Started
  2. Interface Overview
  3. Analysis Types
  4. Advanced Features
  5. Tips & Best Practices
  6. Troubleshooting

docs.title: First Steps
docs.text:
1. Launch the application using streamlit run app/streamlit_app.py
  2. Open your browser to the provided local URL (usually http://localhost:8501)
  3. Choose your analysis type from the sidebar navigation menu

docs.title: Supported Input Formats
docs.text:
• SMILES strings (e.g., CCO for ethanol)
  • CSV files with SMILES column for batch processing
  • Direct text input for multiple molecules

docs.title: Navigation Menu
docs.text:
The sidebar contains the main navigation options:

  • Single Molecule Analysis - Analyze one molecule at a time
  • Batch Analysis - Process multiple molecules simultaneously
  • Molecule Comparison - Compare two or more molecules
  • Conformational Analysis - Study molecular flexibility
  • Advanced Analysis - Drug-likeness and property optimization
  • System Info - Technical information and system status

docs.title: Main Content Area
docs.text: The main area displays: - Input controls for molecular data - Analysis results and visualizations - Interactive charts and 3D models - Export options for data and visualizations

docs.title: Single Molecule Analysis
docs.text:
Purpose: Comprehensive analysis of individual molecules

How to Use: 1. Enter a SMILES string in the input field 2. Click "Analyze Molecule" 3. Review the calculated properties 4. Explore 2D and 3D visualizations

Key Features: - Molecular properties (MW, LogP, TPSA, etc.) - 2D molecular structure - Interactive 3D visualization - Drug-likeness assessment

docs.title: Batch Analysis
docs.text:
Purpose: High-throughput processing of molecular datasets

How to Use: 1. Upload a CSV file with SMILES column 2. Or enter multiple SMILES (one per line) 3. Click "Process Batch" 4. Download results as CSV

Key Features: - Process up to 1000 molecules - Statistical summaries - Property distributions - Batch export capabilities

docs.title: Molecule Comparison
docs.text:
Purpose: Side-by-side analysis of multiple molecules

How to Use: 1. Enter 2-4 SMILES strings 2. Assign names to each molecule 3. Click "Compare Molecules" 4. Analyze differences and similarities

Key Features: - Property comparison tables - Similarity calculations - Overlay visualizations - Radar charts for property profiles

docs.title: Conformational Analysis
docs.text:
Purpose: Study molecular flexibility and conformational changes

How to Use: 1. Enter a SMILES string 2. Set number of conformers (1-50) 3. Choose optimization level 4. Enable "Show Conformational Changes" for advanced visualization

Key Features: - Multiple conformer generation - Energy analysis and plots - 3D conformer visualization - Conformational change labeling with color-coded highlights - Flexibility hotspot identification

docs.title: Advanced Analysis
docs.text:
Purpose: Drug-likeness assessment and molecular optimization

How to Use: 1. Enter a SMILES string 2. Click "Perform Advanced Analysis" 3. Review drug-likeness metrics 4. Explore optimization suggestions

Key Features: - Lipinski's Rule of Five - Veber's Rule compliance - ADMET predictions - Optimization recommendations

docs.title: 3D Visualization Options
docs.text:
Visualization Styles: - Ball and Stick - Standard molecular representation - Space-filling - Van der Waals surface representation - Wireframe - Simplified bond-only view

Bond Type Visualization: - 🔵 Blue bonds - Triple bonds (C≡C, C≡N) - 🟢 Green bonds - Double bonds (C=C, C=O) - 🟣 Purple bonds - Aromatic bonds (benzene rings) - Dark gray bonds - Single bonds (C-C, C-H)

Conformational Change Features: - Shortened hydrogen bonds for better visual proportion - Color-coded change highlighting: - 🔴 Red: Major changes (>2.0 Å displacement) - 🟠 Orange: Minor changes (1.0-2.0 Å displacement) - Interactive conformer comparison - Real-time change analysis

docs.title: Export Options
docs.text:
Available Formats: - JSON - Complete analysis data - CSV - Tabular property data - HTML - Interactive visualizations - PNG - Static images

What You Can Export: - Molecular properties - Analysis results - 3D visualizations - Comparison data

docs.title: State Management
docs.text: The application automatically saves: - Analysis results across sessions - Visualization settings - Input history - Cached calculations

docs.title: Input Preparation
docs.text:
• Validate SMILES before analysis using online checkers
  • Use canonical SMILES for consistency
  • Clean your data before batch processing

docs.title: Performance Optimization
docs.text:
• Limit conformers to 20-30 for complex molecules
  • Use batch processing for multiple molecules
  • Clear cache if memory usage becomes high

docs.title: Visualization Best Practices
docs.text:
• Enable conformational changes for flexibility studies
  • Use appropriate visualization styles for your analysis purpose
  • Save visualizations before clearing results

docs.title: Conformational Analysis Tips
docs.text:
• Start with 10-20 conformers for initial exploration
  • Use higher energy thresholds (5-10 kcal/mol) for diverse conformers
  • Enable change labeling to identify flexible regions
  • Compare low-energy conformers for meaningful analysis

docs.title: Common Issues
docs.text:
"Invalid SMILES" Error: - Check for typos in the SMILES string - Ensure proper syntax (no spaces, correct parentheses) - Try using a different SMILES representation

Slow Performance: - Reduce number of conformers - Clear browser cache - Check system memory usage - Restart the application

Visualization Not Loading: - Refresh the browser page - Check browser compatibility (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge) - Disable browser extensions that might interfere

3D Visualization Issues: - Update your browser to the latest version - Enable hardware acceleration - Try a different visualization style

docs.title: Getting Help
docs.text:
If you encounter issues:

  1. Check the error message for specific guidance
  2. Restart the application to clear temporary issues
  3. Review the troubleshooting section above
  4. Contact support with detailed error descriptions
